clue.text: The underside, or reverse, if in piano

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other word

parts.note: piano is the musical direction meaning soft

indicators.note: reverse tells us the little word if is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describing the bottom of a piano, or the back of one.
explanation.walkthrough: Piano is the musical direction for soft playing; 'reverse' turns if around and 'in' tucks it inside. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A soffit is the architectural term for the exposed underneath surface of an arch, balcony or eave.

clue.text: Discredited pastoral staff found in' Withy Grove?

indicators.note: dis-credited is read as having CR, the usual abbreviation for credit, taken away

parts.note: a crosier is the hooked staff carried by a bishop as shepherd of the flock

explanation.surface: A bishop's crook is disowned and turns up in a Manchester street called Withy Grove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discredited' removes CR (credit) from CROSIER. Withy Grove is a real Manchester street, but here a withy grove is a stand of willows.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiers are the pliant willows whose twigs are called withies, so a grove of withies is full of them.

clue.text: Bluff American racing crew get red in the face

parts.note: a four is a rowing boat with a crew of four oarsmen
to flush is to go red in the face

explanation.surface: A rowing crew is embarrassed, blushing after some American bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker a four-flush is a hand one card short of a flush; to bet on it is to bluff, chiefly in American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To four-flush is US slang for to bluff or make empty pretensions, from betting on an incomplete poker hand.

clue.text: Detail tidy piece of scandal from America

indicators.note: de-tail is read as cutting off the tail, the last letter, of the word tidy

parts.note: a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Someone shares a neat little detail of American gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detail' cuts off the tail of tidy. Tidbit is the American spelling of the British titbit, which is why the definition says from America.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidbit is a choice morsel, often a juicy item of gossip, spelt this way in the US.

clue.text: Repository for leaves which have not been bagged

definitions.text: Repository for leaves which have not been bagged

parts.words: Repository for leaves which have not been bagged
parts.note: the leaves are tea leaves kept loose rather than in teabags, and the repository is the small tin or box holding them

explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is the lidded container in which loose tea is stored at home.

clue.text: Hurling match at the Highland Games?

definitions.text: Hurling match at the Highland Games?

parts.words: Hurling match at the Highland Games?
parts.note: hurling looks like the Irish stick game, but here it means throwing, and the match is the big pole thrown in the Scottish event

explanation.definitionFit: The Highland Games event in which a tall wooden pole is thrown end over end, the pole being a giant matchstick.

clue.text: Words that can be taken in more than one way

definitions.text: Words that can be taken in more than one way

parts.words: Words that can be taken in more than one way
parts.note: the more than one way is reading the lines both horizontally and vertically, as with initial letters spelling a word downward

explanation.definitionFit: In this kind of poem or puzzle the first letters of lines spell a word, so it is read along and down.

clue.text: Everybody is about to read "Coral Island"

indicators.note: is about tells us the first word surrounds the next one

parts.note: all means everybody
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone is about to read the boys' adventure book The Coral Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' wraps everybody around to. The Coral Island is R. M. Ballantyne's Victorian adventure novel, but the definition is any coral island.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped reef or island formed of coral around a lagoon.

clue.text: Insect can turn into land frog, yellow at first

indicators.note: turn into says the letters of the words land frog are changed into a new arrangement
at first takes only the opening letter of the word yellow

explanation.surface: A frog on land, yellow at first, can transform into a flying insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can turn into' rearranges LANDFROG into DRAGONFL, and 'at first' adds Y from yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The dragonfly is a large, fast-flying insect with a long body and two pairs of wings.

clue.text: Smooth with Campbell's rapid roller or blender

parts.note: liquid can mean smooth and flowing, as in a liquid voice
the poet Thomas Campbell's Hohenlinden speaks of the Iser, rolling rapidly

explanation.surface: Something smooth, perhaps involving Campbell's soup, a fast roller or a kitchen blender.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iser (Isar) is the Bavarian river of Campbell's poem Hohenlinden: 'the flow of Iser, rolling rapidly'. Campbell's looks like the soup brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquidiser is the British name for an electric kitchen machine that purees food, a blender.

clue.text: Eggs left for test here

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: Eggs are left out ready for an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground that hosts Test matches, so test here means where a Test is played.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval in Kennington is a cricket ground where England plays Test matches.

clue.text: Reading matter for the wall eyed?

definitions.text: Reading matter for the wall eyed?

parts.words: Reading matter for the wall eyed?
parts.note: wall-eyed is read as having eyes on walls, so the reading matter is what people scrawl on them

explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti are words and drawings painted or scratched on public walls, there to be read by passers-by.

clue.text: This cabin is not convertible

parts.note: the word names both a ship's main cabin and a car with a fixed roof, unlike one whose top folds down

explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is the large public cabin on a liner and also a car body with a fixed hard top.

clue.text: Skirt for the" lily-white boys' number, say

indicators.note: say signals that the number is spoken and we enter what it sounds like

parts.note: in the song Green Grow the Rushes O, two, two are the lily-white boys

explanation.surface: Choosing a skirt for a song performed by some pure-looking boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells us to sound out TWO TWO, the line 'Two, two, the lily-white boys' from the folk song Green Grow the Rushes O.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short, stiff, layered skirt worn by ballerinas.

clue.text: Not a girl turned up without one howling

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the reversed run goes around a letter
in a down clue, turned up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
Lulu is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boy turned up with no partner, wailing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses NOT A LULU to ULULATON, and 'without' wraps that around I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Ululation is a long wailing or howling cry, of grief or celebration.

clue.text: State of ground unsatisfactory — getting hard

parts.note: in horse racing the going is the condition of the turf
off means not up to standard, as in an off day

explanation.surface: A racing report: the turf is in poor shape and firming up.
explanation.walkthrough: Going off is used of concrete, glue or plaster setting hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting concrete or glue is said to go off as it hardens.

clue.text: Large hods may be used in this fuel store

indicators.note: may be used here hints that the letters of large hods are put to use in a new order

explanation.surface: Big builders' hods might be needed at the town gasworks.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasholder is the huge tank, a gasometer, in which town gas is stored for supply.

clue.text: Death by hangings

definitions.meaning: drapes hung at windows or across a stage

explanation.definitionFit: The fall of the drapes ends a play, hence slang for the end of life; the plain sense is window drapes.

clue.text: Unmentionable whist pair

indicators.note: pair calls for the word to be written twice over

parts.note: whist is an old interjection calling for silence, like hush

explanation.surface: Two players at a whist table, sworn to secrecy.
explanation.walkthrough: Whist looks like the card game, but it is an old call for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hush-hush is secret, not to be talked about.

clue.text: In itself a nasty eyesore

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words nasty eyesore

explanation.surface: Something that is, by its very nature, an unpleasant blot on the landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' finds the letters inside 'nasty eyesore'; read as a whole, the clue also describes the thing, a literally sore eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, quite literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: "-- thee from felicity awhile" (Hamlet)

parts.note: the dying Hamlet asks Horatio to stay away from heaven's bliss a little longer, and the missing word opens that line

explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's line uses the word as a verb, asking Horatio to keep himself away from happiness for now.

clue.text: Everyone ready to go outside in tin hat

indicators.note: outside says the first word goes around the other

parts.note: set means ready to go
all means everyone

explanation.surface: All troops prepared, wearing steel helmets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps ready to go around everyone. Tin hat is slang for a soldier's helmet, and the sallet was its medieval ancestor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sallet is a light medieval helmet, the forerunner of the soldier's steel helmet.

clue.text: There is usually a cut in the turnover here

definitions.text: There is usually a cut in the turnover here

parts.words: There is usually a cut in the turnover here
parts.note: turnover sounds like business takings, but it is the folded-back flap of a jacket front, which normally has a notch

explanation.definitionFit: The folded-back front of a jacket collar usually has a notch cut into it.

clue.text: Group accountant's slush fund

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
boodle is slang for money used for bribery or graft

explanation.surface: A firm of accountants keeps a secret fund for bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: Caboodle means a collection or lot, mostly in the phrase the whole caboodle.

clue.text: 50 in-turn give tongue

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50
taken as written
a go is a turn

explanation.surface: Fifty people speak up one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: Give tongue means to speak out, but here tongue alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a language, and a tongue is also a language.

clue.text: Soldier statesman — a trimmer

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A soldier-politician who trims his views to suit.
explanation.walkthrough: A trimmer looks like a turncoat politician, but here it is something used for trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimp is a silk or cotton thread stiffened with wire, used as trimming on dresses and furniture.

clue.text: Engendering fashionable behaviour

parts.note: in means fashionable
breeding is good manners, the behaviour of the well brought up

explanation.surface: Producing the sort of manners that are in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbreeding is producing offspring from closely related parents, a form of engendering.

clue.text: He identifies constituents as nearly as possible

indicators.note: possible hints that the letters of nearly as can form a possible new arrangement

explanation.surface: A chemist identifies ingredients as precisely as he can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges NEARLYAS; 'as' before it is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breaks a substance down into its parts identifies its components.

clue.text: Fish in river going into lake

indicators.note: going into places one word inside the other

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A fish swims in a river flowing into a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarpon is a large silvery game fish of warm Atlantic waters.
